chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Bundar narrated from Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Khorasani, the servant of Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Some of the Zandiqs ( those of divine unity)
He replied: Yes, and He has named Himself with that in His Book.
He said: Say, 'What thing is greater in testimony?' Say, 'God is witness between me and you.'
So He is a Thing for which there is no other thing alike.

key_terms.الزَّنَادِقَة: Zandiqs (a group known for denying divine attributes or claiming corporeality)
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْء: Not like Him is any thing (Quranic phrase)

ai.seo_question: Can God be called a 'thing' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (AS) engages with the Mu'tazilite-influenced debate on divine attributes by affirming that 'Shay'' (thing/entity) is a valid name for God, thereby rejecting the notion that it implies corporeality (*jism*). He supports this by citing Quranic verses where 'Shay'' is used in a general sense, while simultaneously referencing the verse 'There is nothing like Him' to clarify that this 'thingness' is unique and distinct from created entities. This highlights the Shia scholarly approach of balancing linguistic precision with theological nuance to preserve God's transcendence (*tanzih*) without denying His real attributes.
